title: SDK Lightpath — Ops Playbook & Quickstart Blueprint (Draft)
body:
Purpose
This doc is a compact operations-focused playbook for launching a new Redwood SDK distribution (polyglot). The goal is to provide a 3–10 minute dev quickstart, an ops preflight checklist, a minimal telemetry contract, and a safe rollout plan that non-specialist engineers (product/platform) can follow to get a sample app to production-like traffic.

Context & motivation
- We frequently ship SDK updates (API ergonomic changes, telemetry hooks, hotfixes). Teams want a reproducible, low-friction onramp that:
  * gets developers from zero to an instrumented sample app in < 10 minutes,
  * exposes cost/latency tradeoffs,
  * and reduces flaky first impressions (invalid credentials, mismatched model names, streaming issues).
- This playbook focuses on the "lightpath": the shortest, safest path for a new or returning engineer to run a working integration and validate core behaviors.

Audience
- Solutions engineers, SDK maintainers, product engineers doing sample app demos, and the small CS pre-sales team that runs quick PoCs.

Assumptions
- User has a Redwood account with a valid API key.
- Basic local toolchain: Node 18+ and/or Python 3.10+, Git, curl.
- Access to the sample repo (linked above).

Quickstart (3–10 minutes)
1) Clone sample app
   - git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-lightpath-samples.git && cd sdk-lightpath-samples/javascript/quickstart
2) Install and configure
   - npm ci
   - cp .env.example .env && edit .env to add REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...
3) Run dev server / smoke test
   - npm start  # starts local dev server and a tiny demo UI
   - curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/generate -d '{"prompt":"Write a 10-word team standup"}' | jq .
4) Verify streaming and fallback
   - In another terminal run: tail -F logs/dev.log and watch for STREAM_START, STREAM_CHUNK, STREAM_END events.
   - Force a fallback by setting model=legacy-small in .env and confirm the app still responds (albeit slower).

Preflight checklist (before user-facing rollout)
- API compatibility: run integration tests against the public staging endpoint (CI job: dx/integration-staging).
- Telemetry opt-in: confirm sample app defaults to telemetry=false in .env.example; document how to explicitly opt-in.
- Credential handling: sample uses REDWOOD_API_KEY from env; ensure no keys are accidentally committed.
- Rate-limit demo: add a local rate-limit of 10rps in the sample to simulate quota exhaustion.
- Failure injection: CI step that simulates pod restarts and high latency to assert client retries.
- Red-team smoke: quick checklist for legal/compliance for customer-shared demos (PII flows, storage).

Minimal telemetry contract (why we need it)
- Objective: enable rapid troubleshooting without leaking user content. Keep privacy-first.
- Events (atomic, small payloads):
  * sdk.init — timestamp, sdk.version, language, os
  * api.call.start — call_id, model_hint, route, seq_len_estimate, batching_hint
  * api.call.success — call_id, latency_ms, token_count, hardware_tier
  * api.call.error — call_id, error_class, http_status, retry_count
  * streaming.chunk — call_id, bytes, elapsed_ms (optional, sampled)
- PII rules: do NOT send prompt text or model outputs. Only send hashed prompt_id if you need content-level regression tracing (sha256, salted per-org).
- Sampling: default 1% sampling on streaming.chunk and 100% on api.call.error. Allow org override.

Quality gates and acceptance criteria
- Local quickstart: passes smoke test (generate endpoint returns 200 + stable streaming).
- CI: unit tests + integration tests (against staging) must pass.
- Telemetry: events appear in the staging telemetry dashboard within 2 minutes.
- Performance: median cold-start latency < 300ms for the sample workload on Dedicated small tier; 95th < 800ms (measured via synthetic CI).
- Backward compatibility: no breaking public API changes unless flagged in CHANGELOG with migration steps; any breaking change must be behind a feature flag and in a major release window.

Rollout phases (safe expansion)
1) Internal alpha — internal teams only (1–3 teams), telemetry=on for owners. Run for 48hr.
2) Beta — invite + CS demos; monitor telemetry, adjust defaults for batching/kv-cache. Run 7 days.
3) GA sample — make sample repo public, add marketplace listing in docs, create a short tutorial video.

Operational runbook (for quick incidents)
- Symptom: sample app returns 502s / 'stream aborted'
  1) Check API K/V: are keys valid? (curl to /health with key)
  2) Check token quota & rate-limit headers. If quota exhausted, instruct user to switch to test key or reduce rps.
  3) Tail telemetry: look for api.call.error spikes with same error_class. If error is downstream model OOM, switch model_hint to another compatible variant.
  4) If streaming stalls: rotate to non-streaming fallback by toggling STREAMING=false in .env and retry.
- Symptom: excessive cost in demo runs
  * Action: reduce max_tokens to 32 in the sample app, enable prefix/caching suggestions in README.

Examples: sample config snippets
- .env.example minimal
  REDWOOD_API_KEY=
  REDWOOD_MODEL=gpt-small-rlhf
  STREAMING=true
  TELEMETRY=false
  MAX_TOKENS=128

- curl smoke test
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"model":"gpt-small-rlhf","prompt":"List 3 facts about redwood inference"}' | jq .

Troubleshooting notes for maintainers
- Common pitfall: dev machine has an old node-gyp binary causing native module build failures. Add a short helper script ./scripts/fix-dev-prereqs.sh.
- Observability blind spot: when sampling is too aggressive we miss streaming regressions. Increase sampling to 5% for any beta run that focuses on streaming UX.

Open questions (needs owner)
- Do we want telemetry to be opt-out for internal trials? (owner: Product, decision due EOD next sprint)
- Should sample apps include a tiny local mock of the routing/fallback logic to make canary behaviors reproducible? (owner: SDK lead)
- Is there appetite to add a quick 'cost-estimator' that runs against local traces to show expected per-1000-request spend? (owner: PM, backlog)

Next steps (short-term)
- [ ] Add fix-dev-prereqs.sh and a one-liner bootstrap script. (Aisha)
- [ ] Wire the minimal telemetry contract into the JS + Python SDKs with toggles and sampling defaults. (Marco)
- [ ] Run a 48hr internal alpha and collect telemetry; document any friction points. (Riley + CS)

Appendix: smoke test checklist (single-sheet)
- Clone repo, set key -> start server -> hit /api/generate -> streaming observed -> logs show sdk.init and api.call.success -> telemetry events appear in staging dashboard.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally short and pragmatic. The aim is to reduce friction for early demos while protecting user data and giving operators quick signals for problems. Please comment directly in the doc where you want different thresholds, additional telemetry fields, or alternate rollout timing.
